item.title: Grok Build 1.0.89
item.description: Dashboard adds /rename to rename sessions: Several old records sit in the list, and you want to give one a clearer label without opening each one.

item.title: Grok Build 1.0.88
item.description: MCP servers support dynamic request headers: When connecting to external tools, you can let a command provide request headers dynamically instead of hardcoding them in the config.

item.title: Grok Build 1.0.87
item.description: Minimal mode /mcps adds search and action hints: If you prefer working in minimal mode, managing MCP (a protocol that lets AI connect to external tools) connections is no longer cut short.

item.title: Grok Build 1.0.86
item.description: URLs and File Links in Chat Open Effortlessly: Pasting web addresses or organizing local files in chat used to leave you with links you could not open directly.

item.title: Grok Build 1.0.85
item.description: Terminal notifications now fire for questions and plan approvals: When running tasks in the background in your terminal, Grok sometimes pauses to wait for your answer or confirmation on the next step.

item.title: Grok Build 1.0.80
item.description: Narrow terminals no longer clip buttons and info: When opening Grok Build in a split laptop window or a small pane, you no longer have to keep widening the window just to see the whole screen.

item.title: Grok Build 1.0.79
item.description: /rewind works in place for paged sessions: When a conversation grows long and splits across multiple pages, stepping back to an earlier point often meant waiting for the entire history to reload.

item.title: Grok Build 1.0.78
item.description: @ file chips can be edited in place and support new syntax: If you want the AI to read a file but pick the wrong one, you no longer need to delete it and start over.

item.title: Grok Build 1.0.77
item.description: Unidentified terminals support Shift+Enter newlines: Trying to start a new line in a long paragraph often failed because your terminal window wasn't recognized yet.

item.title: Grok Build 1.0.76
item.description: Ctrl+L redraws the screen after a terminal clear without flashing: When you run intensive tasks with Grok Build in the terminal, lengthy output often accumulates on the screen.
